title: State v. A.M. & Ors. (Transit Cargo Logistics Theft / Identity Trap Case)
citation: Sessions Court Special Cargo Crime Registry Docket #C-14/2026
confidence_note: High (Latent friction ridge match and cellular GPS telemetry vs. airport flight alibi)

ground_truth.culprit_summary: Logistics Dispatcher Alok M. (H2, Clean Record)
ground_truth.rationale: Latent fingerprint on container seal and coincident GPS telemetry prove Alok M. committed the cargo theft; prior offender Amarjit S. (H1) is conclusively exonerated by commercial flight records.

hypotheses.label: Former Transporter Amarjit S. (Prior Cargo Hijack Record)
hypotheses.statement: Former long-haul trucker Amarjit S., who has two prior convictions for highway cargo interception, intercepted the logistics container en route.

hypotheses.label: Logistics Depot Dispatcher Alok M. (Clean Record)
hypotheses.statement: Depot logistics dispatcher Alok M. secretly broke the container seal at the intermediate siding and diverted the high-value electronics.

hypotheses.label: Accidental In-Transit Seal Rupture
hypotheses.statement: The container seal snapped accidentally due to road vibration and cargo fell out undetected.

exhibits.name: State Fingerprint Bureau Latent Friction Ridge ACE-V Report
exhibits.text: Latent friction ridge print lifted using cyanoacrylate fuming from the fresh sheared edge of high-security container seal #SL-88902 matched the left index finger of Suspect Alok M. (H2) with 14 clear minutiae points. Suspect Amarjit S. (H1) friction ridge pattern is completely incompatible and excluded.

exhibits.name: GPS Telemetry & Cellular CDR Siding Triangulation
exhibits.text: Cell tower sector logs and FASTag telemetry show Alok M.'s personal vehicle was stationary alongside the container truck at the desolate railway siding for 38 minutes between 01:25 and 02:03 IST. Bluetooth handshake recorded between his vehicle and the depot scanner.

exhibits.name: Air India Passenger Manifest & Airport CISF Biometric Gate Log
exhibits.text: Official certified flight manifest for Air India AI-804 confirms Suspect Amarjit S. (H1) boarded the aircraft at New Delhi (DEL) at 23:45 IST and landed at Bengaluru (BLR) at 02:35 IST. CISF biometric DigiYatra facial recognition timestamps confirm his physical presence aboard the flight throughout the incident window.

exhibits.name: SCRB Certified Criminal Record Dossier for Amarjit S.
exhibits.text: Certified conviction dossier showing Amarjit S. was convicted in 2018 and 2020 under Section 392 IPC for highway transit cargo thefts. Both cases involved tampering with container seals.

adversarial_exhibit.name: Fabricated Siding Log Sheet Entry
adversarial_exhibit.text: Photocopied night register sheet containing a handwritten scribble alleging 'Amarjit truck spotted outside siding gate at 01:30.'

H1.mo_description: Sheared container bolt seal at transit halt and offloaded consumer electronics into waiting mini-truck.
